note: Reference data for subscription tiers, per-provider concurrency, and curated cloud models. Editable: update this file and pull to pick up new plans/models/limits. Copied to bundle/subscriptions.json at build time and read at boot (with an embedded fallback in src/subscriptions.ts). `concurrency` is what the council allows in parallel against that plan; `concurrencyBasis` records where each number comes from — only Ollama publishes hard per-plan caps, Claude/ChatGPT publish usage multipliers over a shared throttled pool, so their values are engineering starting points scaled with the tier multiplier.

chatgpt.concurrencyBasis: OpenAI publishes usage multipliers (Pro = 5x/20x Plus) over a shared pool with fair-use throttling, not a per-plan concurrency. Starting points: Plus = 6 (the Codex CLI's own default child-agent count, chosen upstream partly to avoid HTTP 429), Pro tiers scaled up.

claude.concurrencyBasis: Anthropic publishes rolling usage allowances (Pro at least 5x Free, Max = 5x/20x Pro), not a per-plan simultaneous-session count — concurrent sessions share the plan's pool and can be throttled. Values are engineering starting points scaled with the tier multiplier.

grok.concurrencyBasis: xAI publishes no per-plan concurrency; conservative unverified estimates.

ollama.concurrencyBasis: Published hard caps (ollama.com/pricing): Free 1 / Pro 3 / Max 10 concurrent cloud slots — requests above the cap queue, then reject; cannot be raised client-side. Council keeps Free = local-only even though the plan includes 1 cloud slot, because a single slot would fully serialize a cloud council.
